title: PBMC isolation and cryopreservation
author: Marloes Van Splunter

steps_raw.instruction: Isolation PBMCs leucosep_protocol Work sterile in the flow cabinet Procedure: 1. Collect the blood samples in tubes with sodium heparinate 2. Order the blood donors from low (1) to high (31) donor number and make 2 batches 3. Study day: Fill the Leucosep® tube with the separation medium: 15 mL Ficoll plaque plus RT--> 2 tubes per donor  Ficoll has to be at least Room temperature before using leucosep tubes for PBMC isolation. 4. Close the tubes containing the Ficoll with the screw-cap and centrifuge for 30 seconds at 1000 x g at RT. The separation medium is now located below the porous barrier. 5. Add 9 ml of PBS to the leucosep tubes and make sure the PBS is at RT before adding blood. 6. The tubes are now ready for filling with anticoagulated blood. We use blood:PBS in 2:1 dilution -->Poor the 2 blood tubes per donor into the correct leucosep tubes. One tube contains 8-10 ml so in total we have +/- 30 ml (2 tubes of blood + 9ml PBS) 7. Centrifuge 10 minutes at 1000 x g at RT in a swinging bucket rotor. Switch-off brakes of the centrifuge (deceleration =1, acceleration =3). 8. After centrifugation, the sequence of layers occurs as follows (seen from top to bottom): a) Diluted Plasma b) Enriched fraction (interphase of PBMC’s) c) Separation medium d) Porous barrier e) Separation medium f) Pellet (erythrocytes and granulocytes) 9. Harvest the enriched cell fraction (PBMC’s) by means of a sterile 1ml pipette. Collect the PBMCs into a correctly labelled 50 ml tube 10. Wash the PBMCs by adding RPMI1640 up to 35 ml and centrifuge for 7’ 250 x g 11. Poor the supernatant into a waste bottle and resuspend the PBMCs by flicking the tube to loosen the pellet 12. Repeat washing step twice; resuspend the cell pellet up to a total volume of 10mL with RPMI1640 . 13. After three times washing resuspend the PBMCs in 2 ml of RPMI-1640 medium and count (see NOBLE protocol), before they are ready to use for staining, cell culture or for cryopreservation

Prepare freezing media and cryovials • Cryovials (write them with permanent writer: name, date, concentration (5-
10·106cells/ml) and content) • Prepare the media in the tubes Medium A: 100% FCS Medium B: 20% DMSO & 80% FCS (Final concentrations: 10% DMSO & 90% FCS) • Store the tubes at 4ºC 1. For cryopreservation of PBMCs all the supernatant has to be removed after the third wash of the PBMCs. Or wash once more 7’ 250 x g 2. Cells are resuspended in 1 ml per 10x10^6 PBMCs ice-cold medium A (100% FCS) (10 x 10^6 PBMCs/ml in their 15 ml tube  do this for all donors of one batch 3. Per donor add equal amount (ml) as in point 2. of ice-cold medium B (20% DMSO & 80% FCS) is added to tube while gently mixing by shaking the tube 4. The 1ml of cells suspension are divided over maximum of 4 (correctly labelled) cryovials (if no 4 cryovials can be filled  write down how many vials we have) 5. Do this for all donors of the batch 6. Put the cryovials in a white box  surround with paper towel and put is in a big Styrofoam box  put the entire box with lid in a -80 ºC freezer 7. Place the freezing container in -80ºC freezer for 8-12h (overnight) 8. Transfer the cells to liquid nitrogen or the -160 ºC
